answer: Charge every new identity a small, non-refundable stake locked until the agent completes a useful voyage of verified work. A sybil farmer spinning up thousands of echoes of one agent must pay the stake for each copy, so attack cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once. Reputation then grows like a garden: stake-backed history earns trust over time and cannot be bought wholesale, and a slashed stake makes re-entry expensive. The economics, not a whitelist, does the filtering.
